name: on_depth_amount_clicked
doc:
**Depth AMOUNT-row tap** — caps the tapped depth amount to the user's
side-aware max-available balance, then routes it through
`on_amount_changed` so the single canonical amount-writer runs all the
downstream side-effects exactly once (R-INT-1). Mirrors V1
`SpotTriggerFragment.kt:133-151` `depthViewModel.depthItemAmtLd`
observer (the AMOUNT row, NOT the depth PRICE row — the depth price is
forwarded separately through `on_trigger_price_changed` /
`on_order_price_changed`, matching V1 `setInputPrice`'s EditText-focus
routing which is a Native-only concern).

A1 / A2 (native-layer): the cap is business + numeric logic that MUST
live in Rust. V1 leaked it into Kotlin via `getQuantitySpotBookCal` +
`getAmountDigit` + `OKTNumberF.formatDownToMax`
(`SpotTriggerFragment.kt:143-148`). Here Kotlin only forwards the raw
tapped `amount`; Rust caps + writes state.

SIBLING-DEVIATION (R-MIG-105) vs SpotLimit `on_depth_row_clicked`
(`spot_limit_interactor.rs:3976`):
- SpotLimit's action ALSO sets the depth price (single price input).
SpotTrigger has TWO price inputs (trigger / order) and V1 routes the
price by EditText focus (`setInputPrice`, :118) — a Native-only
decision — so the price-set is intentionally NOT folded in here;
Kotlin forwards it through the existing price actions. Amount-only.
- SpotLimit caps via the 4-way `PureMaxAvailState::Loaded`
(`max_buy/sell_with/without_loan`). SpotTrigger's
`OKTSpotMaxAvailState::Loaded { avail_balance, avail_eq }` carries
only the two raw `SpotMaxAvailResponse` fields (`available` /
`max_size`), so the side pick is done against those two: BUY →
`avail_eq` (=`max_size`), SELL → `avail_balance` (=`available`) —
V1 `getSpotAmtBalance` parity (BUY=maxSize, SELL=available).
- V1 SKIPS the cap entirely in quote-amount mode
(`currentAmtSymbolType == SPOT_TYPE_QUOTE`, :135) — only the price is
set, the amount input untouched. Mirrored: no-op in `Quote` mode.

Reuses the shared pure min `CapDepthAmountUseCase` (R-MIG-066 — the
numeric min already exists in `business::make_order::spot_limit::domain`;
not re-implemented).

doc:
Which symbol domain the positions/assets filter narrows by.

FR-1 replaces today's single "current symbol" checkbox with THREE selectable
types. FR-2 then splits what used to be one boolean into two orthogonal
dimensions, and this enum is only the first of them — "which type is
selected". Whether the filter is actually running is the separate
`symbol_filter_active` flag. The two are deliberately NOT collapsed into an
`Option<OktSymbolDomain>`: "a type is selected but the filter is not active"
is a real, observable state.

An enum rather than a string id because both hosts must dispatch
exhaustively (Swift `switch`, Kotlin `when`); a bare string id would push a
validation/fallback branch into each platform, which is business judgment in
the native layer.

`CurrentSymbol` is the default, which is exactly the shipped behaviour for a
user who has never touched the new control.

The shared `Symbol` suffix is REQUIRED, not incidental: these three names are
the cross-platform contract for this round and are what the Kotlin `when` and
Swift `switch` arms are written against, so the variants are not renamed to
satisfy `enum_variant_names`.

name: get_instrument_filter_list
doc:
Pure read — the instrument list for the requested business line,
used by the Kotlin Fragment to build the instrument filter
chip on the history-order page.

Backed by `BizFacade::get_instruments()` (the documented
instrument-list API; `trait_def.rs:199`), selected per `inst_type`
via `BizFacadeFactory::create_facade`. Returns the full
`InstrumentRecord` set (FFI `uniffi::Record`) so Kotlin can read
`inst_id` for the filter value and `display_id` / `base_ccy` /
`quote_ccy` for the chip label without a second FFI round-trip.

`"FUTURES"` / `"OPTION"` (the API `instType` contract values, see
`guides/07-types-and-enums.md` §5). An empty / unknown `inst_type`
yields an empty list (no facade for that biz line).

This is a side-effect-free list accessor (spec §B "List accessor"),
so it lives in the `#[uniffi::export] impl` rather than the actions
trait, and reads no interactor state.
